name: Simultaneous contrast
summary: Pure colours set side by side so that each one raises the force of the other, with the picture built from the contrast alone.
how: Set a complementary pair side by side in each ring or plane.
Keep each colour pure and unmixed, at full chroma.
Repeat the pair in steps of colour, so that the picture beats like a rhythm.

origin.note: Robert Delaunay builds his Windows pictures from contrasts of pure colour, after the law of Michel-Eugène Chevreul (1839).

adoptions.via: Sonia Delaunay shows simultaneous fabrics and clothes of colour blocks at the Boutique Simultanée in Paris.

sources.title: Michel-Eugène Chevreul, The Principles of Harmony and Contrast of Colours (1839)
